why: Aid is formula need minus formula resources, plus foundation aid and a few smaller payments; need, its allowances and school adjusted valuation are inputs to that arithmetic.
The state share of receipts counts TEEOSA aid among state sources, so the two rise together by construction.
Spending per pupil and its change since 2019-20 are two views of one series.
Basic funding and several allowances are built from districts' past spending, so spending and need move together, and aid follows need.
The levy is the request divided by certified taxable valuation, and unused authority is authority minus the request; both come from the same LC-2 budget form.
School adjusted valuation, taxable valuation, its change and the ag share all describe one tax base.
Proficiency and the scale score come from the same NSCAS tests.
Four- and five-year graduation rates follow the same student cohorts.
The ACT benchmark and composite come from the same test.
Average experience and the share of inexperienced teachers describe the same staff.
Aid per student changes with the student count.
Payroll and all-jobs counts share the same jobs.
Wage level and its change are two views of one series.
Income level and its change are two views of one series.
Migration is a component of population change.
Both describe the same age distribution.
Farm income and livestock sales overlap.
Taxes after credits are taxable valuation × the average rate × the share left after state credits; taxes levied, taxable valuation, the rate and the credit share are the parts of that identity.
Agricultural land's share of taxable valuation drives its share of taxes.
Credits and the school share are shares of the same tax bill.
The state share measures come from the same school receipts, and property tax credits count as state money in them.
School aid and the state share come from the same certification.
